turns.content: Cyclohexanone is treated with bromine under alpha-bromination conditions. Identify product 1 and the position at which bromination occurs.
Product 1 is heated with aqueous sodium hydroxide. Identify the rearrangement and product 2, including its ring size and functional group.
Treat product 2 with thionyl chloride and pyridine. Identify product 3 and state the functional-group transformation.
Before choosing the last reagent, compare the hydride selectivity needed to reduce an acyl chloride only to an aldehyde with the behavior of a stronger hydride that continues to a primary alcohol.
Reduce product 3 with lithium tri-tert-butoxyaluminum hydride. Identify product 4 and explain why the reduction stops at that functional group.
For product 4, identify the symmetry-related positions of the substituted cyclopentane ring and distinguish the aldehydic proton, the substituted-ring methine proton, and the ring methylene protons.
Account for the equivalence of symmetry-related positions and for any nonequivalent hydrogens within the methylene groups. How many chemically distinct proton environments does product 4 have?
List the proton environments by type and verify that the list accounts for every hydrogen in product 4 without double-counting symmetry-related sites.
Check whether conformational averaging of the ring changes the equivalence classes used in the proton count, and reconcile the result with the molecular symmetry.
Give the identity of product 4 and the final number of chemically distinct proton environments, with a concise symmetry explanation.
